service_boundary: Represents the TrustedRouter routing service and its attested gateway, not the upstream providers it forwards to. A small set of house composite models is layered over other providers' models rather than separately trained.
regional_controls: A European routing alias is documented alongside zero-retention and end-to-end aliases; upstream provider selection still determines where processing occurs.
retention_controls: The privacy policy states prompts and outputs are never logged, with an opt-in batch path retaining enclave-encrypted artifacts for up to thirty days. Request metadata is itemised but carries no fixed retention period. Upstream retention is disclaimed twice, and only a minority of catalogue models route to a zero-retention upstream.
routing: Aliases select automatic health-based failover, zero-retention routes, end-to-end encrypted routes, or European routes, and per-request constraints can require a minimum privacy class.
customization: Customer-supplied provider keys are supported on many models; no customer fine-tuning is documented, and the house models are ensembles over existing providers.
strengths: The privacy claim is cryptographically checkable rather than asserted: a live attestation signed by the cloud operator names an image digest matching the published one, and binds the connection's own certificate.
Three confidential-computing planes are documented, with signed trust artifacts recorded in a public transparency log.
Corporate identity is disclosed to an unusual degree, including registration identifiers and a named signatory, in a category where anonymous operators are common.
tradeoffs: The gateway and control plane are published under a source-available licence granting no production use for four years, so the service's own description of the code as fully open is inaccurate.
No third-party audit exists; the operator states its compliance certification is not obtained and its processing addendum is an unsigned draft.
Documented provider coverage is materially higher than the live catalogue supports, and most models do not route to a zero-retention upstream.
The operation rests on one named individual with no disclosed funding, and the trust page links a repository that does not exist.

response_integrity.note: The receipts page states: "Add one header to any chat or responses call and TrustedRouter returns a signed receipt: a compact proof that this exact request produced this exact response, which model and provider served it, and how the upstream was verified." The receipt is signed inside TrustedRouter's attested enclave and binds the response bytes; whether it reaches the upstream model depends on the route's stated verification tier.
response_integrity.scope: TrustedRouter receipts documentation, for the TrustedRouter API

upstream_disclosure.note: The sub-processor page names the downstream model providers individually and states: "Downstream model providers are subprocessors only when customer traffic is routed to them."
upstream_disclosure.scope: TrustedRouter sub-processor list, for the TrustedRouter API

credential_handling.note: The privacy policy states: "Raw API keys are shown once and stored only as protected hashes. BYOK provider credentials are encrypted."
credential_handling.scope: TrustedRouter privacy policy, for the TrustedRouter API

cache_isolation.note: The prompt-caching guide says only that "Provider caches are generally scoped to a provider, account, model, and prompt prefix." It does not say whose provider account a request on TrustedRouter's own credentials is cached under, so it does not establish whether caches are pooled across customers.
cache_isolation.scope: TrustedRouter prompt-caching guide, for the TrustedRouter API

vulnerability_disclosure.note: The legal page states: "Security contact: security@trustedrouter.com."
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: TrustedRouter legal page, for the TrustedRouter API

independent_audit.note: The legal page states: "TrustedRouter does not yet have SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA certification, or a third-party audit report."
